title: Density of C_c^∞(Ω) in L¹(Ω) for real-valued functions (Step 1 of the supplied proof, from the accepted vector-valued density)
statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be open, and let η : ℝ^k → ℝ be Lebesgue-integrable on Ω. Then for every ε > 0 there is a function φ : ℝ^k → ℝ of class C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. smooth, not analytic) with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ Ω (tsupport = closure of the support) such that ∫_Ω |η(w) − φ(w)| dw < ε, where dw is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^k.
lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl k)) (η : Eucl k → ℝ), IsOpen Ω → IntegrableOn η Ω (volume : Measure (Eucl k)) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ φ : Eucl k → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧ tsupport φ ⊆ Ω ∧ ∫ w in Ω, |η w - φ w| ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k)) < ε
